fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Vehicle Parking Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Detached Structure Complexity
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders confirm the correct property from the road.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the driveway so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Mark the driveway entrance with posts or reflective markers to make the single access point clearly visible at night or in low visibility conditions.
• Clear a walking path around the detached structure so responders can reach all sides of it on foot.
• Post the address number visibly on the detached structure so responders can identify it as a separate building on the property.
• Trim back dense vegetation near the rear of the property to open a path for responders moving between the main residence and the detached structure.
• Keep any rear gates or side gates unlocked, or install a knox-box or combination lock, so responders are not delayed gaining access to the rear of the property.
• Designate and keep clear a flat, firm area near the driveway where emergency vehicles can stage without blocking the single access point.
• Remove or relocate parked vehicles from areas that would block the path between the main residence and the detached structure.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Limited Vegetation Separation; Scattered Trees; Open Green Space; Single Access Route; Vegetation Along Driveway; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to create more open space between the trees and the building.
• Trim lower branches on large trees close to the structure so fire cannot climb from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Remove or cut back shrubs and plants that are growing directly against the structure's walls or foundation.
• Separate areas where trees and shrubs are growing together near the structure so there is a visible gap between them.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure where their canopies touch or overlap each other.
• Trim all overhanging branches and cut back vegetation along both sides of the driveway so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep the full length of the single driveway clear of fallen branches, overgrown shrubs, and any debris that could block a vehicle.
• Mow or cut low vegetation along the driveway edges regularly to reduce plant material that could carry fire toward the structure.
• Remove dead branches, dry leaf litter, and loose plant debris from around the base of trees and shrubs near the structure.
• Keep the open green space near the structure mowed short and free of accumulated dead plant material.
